Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)
Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)
General information
Who can I contact if I have any further questions?
Please feel free to contact our coordination team (mattertolife@maxplanckschools.de)!
How can I stay up to date with the program?
Follow us on Instagram @mps_mattertolife!
Follow us on Bluesky ‪@mattertolife.bsky.social‬!
Follow us on LinkedIn @Max Planck School Matter to Life!
Which specific degree will I obtain upon completing the program?
You will start the program with the 1st phase, a 2-year joint Master program, at Göttingen and Heidelberg universities. If you decide to leave the program after this phase, you will have a Master of Science degree. If you decide to continue to the 2nd phase with a 3-year PhD, you will graduate with the German equivalent of a PhD, a Dr. rer nat, which is recognized worldwide as a PhD.
When does the application portal open, when is the deadline and where can I apply?
The online application portal opens on September 1st, 2026 for admission in 2027. Application is possible until December 1st, 2026 (11:59 pm). The link to the portal is available on the application page. See the program page for more details about the foci offered at each university.
What are the research areas of the Max Planck School Matter to Life?
Our research areas are as diverse as our Faculty which is distributed among the premier institutes and universities in Germany. A common theme that binds different groups within the MtL family is their focus on unraveling the physical and chemical fundamentals of cellular and biological processes to arrive at a greater understanding of the complexities of life. Visit the websites of the faculty members to learn more about their research.
Why should I apply to the Max Planck School Matter to Life (MPS MtL)?
If you are interested in conducting interdisciplinary research, this is your chance to join a prestigious network of top scientists across diverse disciplines, united in their mission to unravel the fundamental concepts of life.
Do I need a visa to study in Germany?
Depending on your nationality and passport you are holding, you would need a visa to enter Germany and/or a residence permit for carrying out your studies. Please check the respective pages from the Auswärtige Amt.
Language proficiency
Is the MPS MtL program offered in English?
Yes, the official language of the school is English and therefore, all courses, events, and communication are in English.
English is not my native language. Am I required to take an English language exam and provide proof of proficiency?
Yes, solid knowledge of the English language is necessary for your success in the program, which will be conducted entirely in English. An internationally-accepted language test will be required for non-native English speakers. Test scores cannot be older than four years prior to the date of application.
Please note: The English language test is required for admission to the program, but not for the application submission. If you cannot complete the test before applying, please indicate that it will be taken at a later date. Your test must be submitted by July 15th of the year you start the program.
The accepted tests are:
TOEFL Paper based 570 out of 677 points
TOEFL internetbased (IBT) - minimum 90 out of 120 points
IELTS - In person or online; minimum band score of 6.5
UNIcert® - minimum UNIcert® II with a minimum grade of 2.3
NULTE - minimum B2+
Cambridge Certificate in Advanced English (CAE) - minimum grade C1
We also accept at least two years of relevant study or professional stay in an English speaking country or successful completion of a study program (Bachelor's or Master's) where the language of instruction was only English within the three years prior to the application submission as proof of English proficiency. This needs to be stated on your certificate/ transcrips or additionally confirmed by your previous institute.
Do I need to learn German for the program?
No! The program will be conducted entirely in English.
Prerequisites for admission
What are the admission requirements?
To be eligible to apply for the program, you must have completed or will complete one of the following by beginning of the study program:
Bachelor of Science degree in Natural Sciences (e.g. in Chemistry, Physics, Molecular Biology, Biochemistry, Materials Science, Biotechnology)
Bachelor of Engineering in a relevant subject (e.g. in the subjects Molecular Systems Engineering, Bioengineering)
or have completed a course of study in a related natural science or engineering discipline in a minimum of six semesters or three academic years
Proof of an above-average Bachelor's degree, demonstrated by either a minimum GPA of 1.7 or evidence that you ranked in the top 5 % of your graduating class. Please note that we do not calculate the GPA before the application deadline as this is done as part of the application review process.
50 % of the credit points obtained during your degree program must be from subjects related to Natural Sciences including mathematics. Of these, 1/3rd should be in physics, chemistry and/or mathematics. For example if your degree program consists of 180 credits, 90 credits should be in Natural Sciences, and 30 of this should be in physics, chemistry and/or mathematics
You have to submit copies of your official transcripts (either in German or English). If your certificates have been awarded by a foreign educational institution, you need to provide certified copies. Additionally, if the certificates are neither in German nor English, official translations must be attached. The relevance of your previous study will be evaluated on a case-by-case basis depending on your transcript and the specific modules/ courses you have completed.
Your application also needs to include a letter of motivation which needs to be filled out directly within the application portal. You can find the form in the tab "Letter of Motivation". Please only use this template; individual letters of motivation will not be accepted.
You will need to meet the minimum score requirements on an approved English language exam. The English proficiency test can be submitted after the selection process is completed (latest until 15 July, 2027 for the current selection phase). Exceptions are, if your native language is English or your previous program was taught in English. In this case you do not need to present the language test, but please provide proof of it. For further details, please refer to the section above on English proficiency.
Do I need to calculate my GPA myself before applying?
No, you do not need to calculate your GPA before submitting your application. We review and calculate your GPA as part of our application review process after the application deadline.
What degree should I have in order to apply to the Max Planck School Matter to Life?
We invite undergraduate students with a background in Physics, Chemistry, Biology, Biotechnology, Materials Science or Engineering (or a related sub-field) to apply to our program. Your previous study (Bachelor of Science, Bachelor of Engineering, Bachelor of Technology, Bachelor of Arts, Staatsexamen etc.) needs to have the equivalent of 180 ECTS.
Please do not send us your transcripts via email for preliminary check. We cannot provide individual feedback based on your transcripts and assess your eligibility. Please submit your application through our portal upon which it will be reviewed.
Can I apply even though I have not yet completed my current academic degree?
Yes, you can apply with a current transcript. You must provide the final transcript and graduation certificate by the time of enrollment to the program.
I have a Master's degree, am I eligible to apply?
Yes, but please note that you still need to complete the Masters in our study program, and credits from your previous study program cannot be transferred.
You will be required to participate in the full 5-year program, of which the first 2 years will consist of university coursework. The qualifying degree is the Bachelor’s degree, but modules taken during a Master degree can be taken into account when evaluating your eligibility during application, and calculating your ECTS.
I have both a Bachelors and Masters. In this case, what is the qualifying degree?
If you have a Bachelors and Masters, the qualifying degree is the Bachelor’s degree in most cases. There are certain countries (Eg. Nepal) where Masters is the qualifying degree. You can check the DAAD website to find out what is applicable for you. This information is for guidance only, and final decision lies with the admission office of the universities.
Modules taken during a Master degree will however be taken into account when calculating your credits, and evaluating your eligibility during application.
I have more than one degree. Which grade will be taken into account?
If you have multiple Bachelors the degree most relevant to our program will be considered. If you have a Bachelors and Masters, the grade from Bachelors will be considered unless the Masters is the qualifying degree.
Do applicants without a Master's degree have an advantage?
No.
How old can the degree be? Are there any limitations?
There are no limitations on the time elapsed after your last degree. You should be able to explain why you have decided to apply for university studies again (especially after a longer gap) and why you seek to do a Master/ PhD in Matter to Life in your motivation letter.
What do you look for in applicants?
We look for applicants with an excellent educational qualifications and high passion for interdisciplinary science.
Does having publications carry additional weight?
Not necessarily. You can refer to your publication in the interviews during the selection process and use them to demonstrate your suitability for the program.
Is research experience required?
Research experience is not required, but could be an advantage. If you already have experience in research, please indicate it in your letter of motivation.
Application process
When can I apply?
Please apply during the application time (September 1st – December 1st) via our application portal to Matter to Life. The link to the application portal and further information on the application process can be found here .
How does the application process work?
Applying to the Max Planck School Matter to Life is done through an online application portal; the link will be provided on our application page. If you are accessing the portal for the first time, you need to first create an account and choose “Max Planck School Matter to Life - Graduate Program”. Please see the application page for more details as well as the link to the portal.
What are the different stages of the application process?
1) Your application will be reviewed by the admission committee who will consider your grades and your suitability for the program based on your transcript and motivation letter.
2) Suitable candidates will be invited for a video conference interview to further assess your motivation and suitability for the program.
3) Candidates who progress to this round will be invited for a second round of interviews where you will discuss 1 to 2 publications from the Matter to Life Faculty. This will be sent to you beforehand.
Based on the evaluation of all three stages, the final top twenty candidates will be selected.
Who are the interviewers?
Your interviews will be conducted by Matter to Life Fellows. You can find a list of our Faculty on our website.
How long are the interviews?
The interviews are about 15 min for the first round and 30 min for the second round.
Do I need to contact the universities directly or just apply via the portal?
Please only apply via the application portal.
Are there separate quotas for applications from Germany and abroad?
We do not have quotas for the Matter to Life study. All applicants will be treated equally irrespective of age, gender, nationality, etc.
Is it possible to apply to both universities?
No, this is a joint degree program; you only need to submit one application.
Is it possible to delay the entry into the program by one year upon acceptance?
Unfortunately not. The application and selection phase of each year are treated independently and you have to reapply if you cannot enter the program at the time you are accepted.
How many students are admitted?
We are aiming for a small cohort size. Therefore, we only accept 20 students per year.
How do I organize everything once I am accepted to the program?
The coordination office will support you with your process and your transition to Germany and the study program. You will also be assigned a buddy from the previous cohort to help you in this process. We will inform you about all the steps you need to take in advance.
Is an application to different Max Planck Schools possible?
Yes. The schools have independent application processes. Make sure to also apply to the other schools separately. Applications will be treated independently.
Application Documents
Which documents are required for the application?
Originals of certificates/Diplomas of all higher education degrees obtained (e.g. B.Sc., etc.) - if already obtained, either in English or German.#
Proof of current enrollment if undergraduate degree is still ongoing (official statement and/or transcript), either in English or German.
Original or official transcripts of completed and/or ongoing degrees, either in English or German.#
Letter of motivation – to be filled out directly within the application portal using the template provided
For non-native English speakers, English language proficiency must be demonstrated by one of the following English language tests or applicable study: TOEFL iBT, IELTS, UNIcert®, NULTE, Cambridge Certificate of Advanced English OR proof of completion of an English language bachelor program or proof of at least two years of relevant study/stay in an English language program in the three years prior to the application deadline. Tests are valid for four years prior to the last date of application submission.*
# Scanned copies of originals are accepted. Unofficial transcripts are not accepted, and your application will be rejected.
* Please note that the English language test is not required for application submission, but is required for acceptance into the program. Therefore, you can complete your application without this document. However, if you are accepted into the program, test scores must be submitted by July 15th, 2027.
My documents are not in English or German. What are certified translations?
Transcripts and Degree certificates are only accepted in German or English. In case they are in any other language, please submit certified translations along with the originals.
Certified translations include:
Translations issued by your university directly
Translations by a sworn translator (vereidigter Übersetzer) in Germany
Translations issued by a translator who is officially recognised in another country
Translations certified by a German embassy or consulate (if permitted in that country).
These are not accepted as certified translations:
Self-translations OR Translations prepared by relatives or friends.
Notarised copies of an unofficial translation.
Machine translations (for example, Google Translate or DeepL).
Do I need to contact you or professors to increase my chances for acceptance?
Contacting us or the professors will not alter your chance of acceptance. However, if you have any questions or uncertainties regarding the program or the application process, you are welcome to always contact the coordination office. We are happy to help.
Will I still be accepted if the Bachelor is not finished prior to the start of the program?
No. All admitted students must have completed their Bachelor’s degree prior to the start of the program. You need to submit proof of a completed Bachelor’s degree to fully enroll at the universities.
What documents are accepted as proof of Top 5%?
Either a rank list from your University demonstrating the same OR a letter from the University/ Dean of your faculty stating that you are in the top 5% will be accepted as a proof. We cannot accept any self-declarations or recommendation letters from Professors/ lecturers in lieu of this.
Are grades judged according to the German grading system?
Your grades will be converted to the German grading system based on the modified Bavarian formula. Therefore, you have to submit the grading scheme of your university.
My university has a very specific grading system; what additional documents should I provide?
You will need to upload the Grading Scheme and Program Curriculum. We encourage all international applicants to upload this so that we can convert your grade to the German grading system. This document should be in either German or English. In case of any other languages, please upload the original AND translated (either German or English); self-translations are accepted only for these documents.
Are all subjects on the transcript taken into consideration, or only the most relevant subjects?
All your grades are taken into account since your final grade will be used for the conversion into the German grading scheme.
Are there any age limitations for applicants?
No, there is no age limitation for applicants. Age is not relevant for the selection process.
My University does not follow the ECTS systems, so my transcript does not have this information. What should I do?
In this case, while filling out the application, you will be asked to give the following information: Duration of your study program and minimum number of credits (or whichever units your university follows) required to graduate from your program. Please fill these out carefully; based on this and your transcripts we will do the ECTS conversion.
Is it sufficient to submit a PDF with my grades as a substitute for transcripts?
No, unfortunately not. You have to either submit a preliminary transcript (a pdf version of your transcript is sufficient) or the final transcript issued from your educational institution.
Do I need recommendation letters?
No. Please do not submit recommendation letters. They will not be taken into account.
Do I need to send a transcript of all my academic background or the transcript of the degree which I base my application on?
Transcripts from your undergraduate qualifying degree (e.g. Bachelor of Science) are compulsory. If you have further relevant qualifications, please also include these.
I received my educational certificate from China - do I need a verification by the Academic Evaluation Center (APS)?
Yes, please also submit the verification by the Academic Evaluation Center (APS).
I received my educational certificate from Hong Kong - do I need a verification by the Academic Evaluation Center (APS)?
No, you do not need to submit a verification by the Academic Evaluation Center (APS). T
I received my educational certificate from Macau - do I need a verification by the Academic Evaluation Center (APS)?
No, you do not need to submit a verification by the Academic Evaluation Center (APS).
I received my educational certificate from Taiwan - do I need a verification by the Academic Evaluation Center (APS)?
No, you do not need to submit a verification by the Academic Evaluation Center (APS).
I received my educational certificate from India - do I need a verification by the Academic Evaluation Center (APS)?
Yes, please also submit the verification by the Academic Evaluation Center (APS).
I received my educational certificate from Vietnam - do I need a verification by the Academic Evaluation Center (APS)?
Yes, please also submit the verification by the Academic Evaluation Center (APS).
Study phase
Funding
What financial support does the Max Planck School Matter to Life provide?
The Max Planck School Matter to Life offers full funding for up to five years. This funding allows you to focus entirely on your scientific work.
During the Master’s Phase, our PhD candidates receive receive a stipend of 1,565 € plus additional support for health insurance (if applicable; max. 100 €) that covers cost of living (including tuition and fees).
Upon successful completion of the Master’s phase, our candidates receive a contract in the PhD Phase in accordance with the local Wage Agreement for Public Service (TVöD/TV-L, E 13), ensuring both academic freedom and financial security.
Other useful general information about finances in Germany can also be found here.
What is the duration of the stipend?
The stipend for the Master’s phase is valid for 2 years.
Accommodation
Do the students tend to get accommodation together?
In Göttingen, you will have the possibility to live in the “Wissenschaftliches Begegnungszentrum” together for the first 6 months, if you wish. In Heidelberg, you can have a room in the student housing of the University Heidelberg. Unfortunately, we cannot guarantee that your flats/rooms are close to each other. Of course, you always have the possibility to look for a room or shared flat on your own.
Is there support from the respective Universities in arranging accommodation?
We will help you to arrange the accommodation for the first 6 months, if required.
Study load
How much time is spent on theoretical coursework, traditional experiments, and computational simulation during the Master study?
That depends on your focus. In general, the curriculum includes roughly 50% lab work if you decide on it. During the first two terms, you will focus more on lectures, followed by a term of lab rotations and the Master thesis. You will have some computational courses in the lecture phase. However, it depends on you what you choose for your lab rotation (of course you could also choose to do computational work) and your Master thesis.
How much mathematical background is needed?
Matter to Life is a quantitative study program so some mathematical background is necessary for you to be able to successfully participate. We offer a voluntary mathematical preparation course for those who like to refresh their knowledge of mathematics.
What type of exams are there?
Depending on the courses you will mostly have one written exam at the end of each lecture or module. Less often you will have an oral exam or an essay.
During which semester do I have to do the Master thesis?
The Master thesis is generally planned for the 4th semester.
Courses/Topics
Which courses will be offered?
Please check the master's phase and find all information in the module handbook.
Are there differences between the universities?
Yes. The Matter to Life program at each University has a specific focus. For Matter to Life at the University of Göttingen this is Complex Systems and Biological Physics, for Matter to Life at Heidelberg University this is Molecular Systems Chemistry and Engineering. However, both sites also share the same courses in the 1st semester to ensure an insight into all disciplines.
How are lab rotations and research mentorship organized?
For the lab rotations, the Faculty members offer cooperative project proposals, from which you can choose. If you have your own research idea, you can also define a project based on this idea together with two Faculty members working on related topics. For the Master thesis and the 2nd research phase in Matter to Life you will have to approach the Faculty members yourself upon finishing the Master, if you have interest in their supervision. Please do not contact the Faculty members before you are admitted to the program. There will be a timeframe for initiating your lab rotation projects, about which you will be informed beforehand.
How much is generally done online?
Most of the focus lectures are held in-person, the shared lectures will be broadcasted from the respective lecture site to the other study sites. This is a hybrid in-person/online format. Almost all lectures are additionally recorded so that students have the possibility to re-watch the lecture content and study particular aspects of their interest in greater depth. Our virtual campus allows you both; to access the lecture content and work together with your peers at both teaching sites.
What happens at the MtL Days?
The MtL Days take place twice a year and are two-day Mini-symposia giving you an insight into Matter to Life research and more defined focus talks on cutting-edge scientific questions. Moreover, we offer discussion opportunities with your peers and the Faculty members.
Transition to research phase
Can the first phase be skipped?
No. We are offering a 5-year MSc to PhD direct track. The Master phase will give you the foundation for a successful research phase in interdisciplinary research and can therefore not be skipped.
I am interested in doing a Master's degree, but I am unsure if I want to commit to the full 5-year PhD program. Can I exit the program after completing the MSc degree?
Yes; while we encourage promising scientists to advance into the research phase (years 3-5) after obtaining their Master's degree (years 1-2), we understand that 5 years is a big commitment to early career scientists; thus, candidates have the option to exit the program after completion of the Master's degree. The program automatically enrolls you in the full 5-year program, so if you choose to continue to the PhD research phase after completion of the MSc, you will not have to re-apply.
Research phase
Am I guaranteed a PhD position after I complete the study phase?
Yes. We have mild prerequisites you still have to fulfill - like you need to find a supervisor within the Matter to Life faculty and obtain a GPA of at least 2.0 in the Master. But besides this, we are looking forward to having you for 3 more years with us (directly following the master's program)!
Which financial support will I receive in the research phase?
During your 3-year research phase you will receive a contract according to the local Wage Agreement for Public Service.
What are the career prospects of MtL graduates?
The scientific network you will have access to gives you excellent opportunities to establish yourself as a scientist. Furthermore, the PhD will prepare you to develop your own research ideas and hone your project management skills. If you decide against a career in academic research, your training to work at a high level in an interdisciplinary field will be an advantage in industrial R & D positions.
Could potential future employers be confused by the term "Matter to Life"?
We expect that employers will recognize the knowledge and skills you have acquired during the first phase, especially your strengths in working in an interdisciplinary environment. Employers will recognize a PhD as a high-level qualification, which prepares candidates for a scientific career in academia or industry.
